resources.string: Where your movies, TV shows, music and photos are: network shares (NAS, PC) and the box\'s own drives. Add a folder once, CineFuze scans it.
Extra catalogs and streams from the internet: Stremio add-ons or CineFuze add-on files. They show in the Add-ons tab.
Changing it downloads the titles, plots and posters of the whole library again, in the new language.
Your own walls, such as Kids or Concerts, made of the sources you pick; each can have a tab of its own in the top menu.
How the movies and TV shows walls look. Pick the one that suits your screen; you can change it back any time.
More room for the posters: the top menu stays hidden until you press Up on the first row or Back.
Keeps the movies wall shorter: the parts of a series take one tile instead of one tile each.
Hide the tabs you never use (Music or Photos, say) to keep the top menu short; your own categories can be shown here too.
The language of CineFuze\'s menus, whatever the box\'s own language is. The movie data\'s language is the TMDB language.
For comparing: shows what the Dolby Vision FEL layer adds to the picture. Leave it off for normal watching.
How 3D Blu-ray movies (MVC) are decoded on this box. Software is the default; switch if a 3D movie does not play well.
Pick your language and movies start with that audio track whenever the file has one.
Pick a language to get its subtitles from the start, or Off for no subtitles at all.
Handy when you understand the movie\'s language: you still get subtitles for the lines spoken in other languages.
Bigger subtitles for a seat far from the screen, or smaller ones that cover less of the picture.
A background behind the subtitle lines keeps them readable on bright scenes.
The color of text subtitles (SRT and the like); some find yellow easier to read than white.
Only videos shot on an iPhone in Dolby Vision are affected; movies are not.
The small pictures over the seek bar while you skip forward or back in a movie.
On: a movie\'s page plays its trailer in the background, as streaming services do. Off: a quiet page.
Turn it down if the trailers are too loud while you browse.
Which player plays your movies: CineFuze\'s own, or the Dune\'s built-in player with its own menus and settings.
Turn it on when an AV receiver or a soundbar decodes the sound. Turn it off if you hear nothing or noise.
Turn off a format your receiver does not handle well: that format then plays as PCM.
Pick the box if TrueHD movies are silent; pick the TV / amplifier for Dolby Atmos.
For hi-res music: the receiver gets each track at its own sample rate. Turn it off if your receiver has trouble with it.
How the photos change in the slideshow. The list shows each style live, with your newest photos.
Music while the slideshow plays, from your own music library.
An old-film look for the slideshow; your photos themselves are not changed.
With more boxes at home: a movie stopped on one continues on the other where you left off.
The name the other boxes list this box under in their sync status.
News, release notes, questions and bug reports (Issues) on GitHub.
CineFuze also looks by itself at start; here you can look right now and install the new version.
Scans every source again now: new files show up, deleted ones go. Needed only for sources without auto refresh.
Brings back the movies and TV shows you hid from the walls.
Your IPTV playlists (M3U, Xtream Codes, One TV) for the Live TV tab.
On: new and deleted files in this folder show on the walls by themselves, with no Refresh the library needed.
On: the folder\'s movies and TV shows show only in the categories that use it (Kids, say), not on the main Movies, TV shows walls.
For Blu-ray folders and ISOs: the Dune\'s own Blu-ray player opens them over NFS. Empty: the share\'s name is used.
Finds the SMB servers (NAS, PC) on the network: open a folder and add it with its type of content.
A USB drive or disk in the box: open a folder and add it with its type of content.
What the folder holds: movies, TV shows, other videos, photos or music. OK changes it.
Checks the server, the share and the login before you add the source.
Opens the category\'s wall, even when it has no tab in the top menu.
Loads the category into the form below: change its name, type or sources, then Save.
On: the category has a tab of its own in the top menu. Off: open it from this page.
What the category shows: movies, TV shows, other videos, photos or music. Only the sources that hold it are listed.
✓: the titles of this source are in the category. A category can take them from several sources.
Adds a new folder right to this category, set to Categories only: its titles stay off the main walls.
Off: the add-on stays installed, but its catalogs and streams are not used.
On: the add-on\'s catalogs get a tab of their own in the top menu instead of being in the Add-ons tab.
Moves it one place up: the add-ons higher in the list come first.
Loads the add-on again from its address, with its newest catalogs.
Some add-ons play only with your account at their service (a subscription, say).
Type the add-on\'s address, or pick an add-on file with the buttons below.
Picks a CineFuze add-on file from a network share or from the box\'s drives.
Loads the channels and the program guide of every playlist again now.
How past programs are asked from the provider. Leave it on automatic; try another one if the archive does not play.
M3U: a playlist address from your provider. Xtream Codes: a server with a user and a password. One TV: your One account.
The program guide\'s address (XMLTV), if your provider gives it apart from the playlist.
Loads the channels once to check the address and the login, without adding the playlist.
